BIOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell Structure and Specialisation? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell Structure and Specialisation.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cell Structure and Specialisation.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell Structure and Specialisation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell Structure and Specialisation.

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. joule (J)

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cell Structure and Specialisation 1.4 Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiolo.

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Biology? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Biology.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Biology.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Biology.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Biology.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Specimen Collection and Preservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Specimen Collection and Preservation.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Specimen Collection and Preservation.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Specimen Collection and Preservation.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Specimen Collection and Preservation.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transport.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transport.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Transport.

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange and Respiration? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange and Respiration.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition 2.2 Transport 2.3 Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Phy.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Biology 1.2 Specimen Collection and Preservation 1.3 Cell Struct.

16. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

17. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo.

19. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Tertiary consumers

20. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Chemicals of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Chemicals of Life.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Chemicals of Life.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Chemicals of Life.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Chemicals of Life.

22. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Gaseous Exchange and Respiration 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Nutri.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Cell Structure and Specialisation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Chemicals of life 2.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Plants 2.1 Nutrition 2.2 Transpo and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Chemicals of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

27. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

28. In three clear sentences, explain Transport and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

30. In three clear sentences, explain Gaseous Exchange and Respiration and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
